_about: Source for gallery.html and tools.html (rendered by feed.js). Only finished, reachable work belongs here. kind: gallery | tool. status: live (a page a stranger can open) | repo (public source) | private (named, walkthrough on request). Order is the order shown. Evidence: dissemblage.art vitrine and each subdomain fetched 2026-11-06 (all 200); GitHub/GitLab listings fetched 2026-11-06. era: ai (prominent, in the feed) | earlier (compressed under a fold). status offline: real work whose host is currently down. thumb: thumbs/<slug>.jpg, captured 2026-11-06 with headless Chrome.

items.name: Enfilade
items.line: First-person inside the {4,3,5} honeycomb of hyperbolic 3-space: five cubic rooms about every edge, doorways aligned to infinity in every direction. Light rays are true geodesics; walk, and the excess of space unfolds.

items.name: Cascade
items.line: Böröczky's binary tiling: congruent rooms, one parent above, four children below, forever. No arrangement of these rooms admits any translational symmetry. An aperiodic order you fall through, doubling at every level.

items.name: Psychic Mirrorscape
items.line: Twenty-two arcana, each drawn as generative art. Keep the ones that pull at you; it measures not only what you chose but how, the pressure and velocity behind the flick, and reads the spread back to you.

items.name: Fixations of the Arcana
items.line: Not a deck but an instrument. Twenty-two cards run through a synthetic scanpath model (saliency, inhibition of return, saccade amplitude) and rendered as leaded glass. Eight parameters, six layers, and the SVG is yours.

items.name: Arcana Spread
items.line: A seven-screen guided reading. Answer each card, name what held your eye, then accept or refuse the threads it proposes between them. The trace of those choices becomes the reading you take away.

items.name: Arcana Recall
items.line: Eight pairs dealt fresh from the twenty-two, face down. Tap to mirror one against its twin: the same glass-facet engine as Mirrorscape, rendered still instead of adrift, revealed instead of drawn.

items.name: The landing loop
items.line: The page you came from: a seeded hypergraph on an eight-second phase clock. It breathes, its filaments carry light, dust drifts through it, and the loop closes to the pixel because every motion is an integer harmonic of one phase.

items.name: H³ ālāp
items.line: A rāga walked along the struts of a Coxeter lattice, over a tanpura. Drag to turn the lattice; tap a note on the rail to send the voice there, or tap toward a bright strut to steer.

items.name: GRAVITY//MAZE
items.line: A dodecahedral toy. A small world, one way out: the rover follows the direction of the field, one cell at a time through etched corridors. Walls hold. The route is fixed.

items.name: hyperstitious.art
items.line: The studio. A hyperstition is an idea that makes itself real by being built; this is where they get built. Generative, interactive and sonic works: less gallery, more workshop.

items.name: The Vitrine
items.line: The lobby for all of the above. Every deck behind it is one HTML file with no build step and no dependency on its siblings: open one and it runs; save it and it still runs in ten years. Nothing phones home.

items.name: co-loop
items.line: A seed repository for agentic collaboration between forks. Fork it, run your agent flow, then merge, branch and pull across forks without stepping on each other's files. The how behind this site's why.

items.name: pi-harness
items.line: Custody of a coding agent: a pinned, checksum-verified install, versioned configuration and doctrine, and one command that proves it still works. Eleven behaviour probes and an A/B bench for prompt and gate changes (n=3, one model: enough to see a change, not to claim a better outcome).

items.name: tidy-harness
items.line: A small LLM harness core in Swift, built from evidence: conformance tests run against real session logs rather than imagined ones.

items.name: free-llm-harness
items.line: A reliability harness for routing across free OpenRouter models: retries, tool loops, quota probes. The 88-request measurement on the CV comes from here.

items.name: api.hyle.lol
items.line: A Rust/Axum proxy in front of OpenRouter with per-client rate limits, an audit log and SSE relay. Meant to live at hyle.lol; the host is down as of 2026-11-06, so it is listed as what it is, not as live.

items.name: The doctrine
items.line: WISDOM, AGENTS and LIFECYCLE: the short, versioned rule set every agent session here reads first. Six load-bearing rules, thirty-eight lessons each tied to a real failure, and twelve lifecycle gates. Private until it is published.

items.name: Agent configurations
items.line: Reproducible configuration for three agents: pi (the custody repo above), Hermes (soul, skills, provider fallback) and opencode (a local LM Studio fallback provider). Configuration, not software of my own; kept so a machine can be rebuilt in an hour.

items.name: Pick Your Poison
items.line: Twenty forks of temperament: terse or thorough, warm or cool, sparring partner or right hand. Swipe them and it writes the system prompt you just described.

items.name: AGENTS.md Forge
items.line: The same twenty axes, aimed at a file. Names itself, groups your answers into voice, work and collaboration, and hands you an AGENTS.md to drop into a project root.

items.name: The Substrate Forge
items.line: Sixteen infrastructure decisions, stateful or stateless, hosted or self-run, RAG or full transcript, cast into a DEPLOY.md you could actually hand to someone.

items.name: The Strand Forge
items.line: Twenty forks between folklore and a load-bearing project. Scores the trade you made as a rigor/velocity tuple, then emits a charter, a NEEDS ledger, and the gates a machine can check for you.

items.name: job-sift
items.line: A Rust CLI that scores live RemoteOK and Hacker News “Who is hiring?” listings against a weighted skill profile, to surface contract-shaped work worth an hour of looking.

items.name: inference_harness
items.line: An Elixir/OTP harness for LLM jobs: multi-provider routing, role-specific fallback chains, time budgets and retry ceilings, a token and latency ledger, bounded concurrency.

items.name: gemini-gate
items.line: A small Elixir/Phoenix credential vault and Gemini API proxy: authenticated retrieval, constant-time token comparison, atomic credential replacement, deployed under Caddy and systemd.

items.name: corpora
items.line: A native macOS app for browsing, searching and composing context from AI conversation history: live ingestion, provenance per artifact, a corpus you can actually find things in.

items.name: Umbra
items.line: A hyperbolic workspace: notes as nodes on the Poincaré disk, Klein model or tree, with a command palette, inspector and link mode. Room for more than a flat canvas can hold.

items.name: Pocket
items.line: Small apps that work offline, installable to a phone home screen: a draft chat traced in ink, a relay messenger with an honest outbox, flip-cards, runnable loops.

items.name: ledger
items.line: A humble, no-frills in-browser knowledge base for project notes, entities, relations and prompt snippets. LocalStorage plus JSON export and import; nothing leaves the page.

items.name: lab.dissemblage.art
items.line: The tooling bench: command-line tools, fleet plumbing and data instruments. Unglamorous and load-bearing, the small sharp things that make the rest of the work possible.

items.name: nixbloom
items.line: An ephemeral NixOS-based workspace: reproducible development environments that come up clean and leave nothing behind.

items.name: market-monitoring
items.line: Market monitoring demo.

items.name: harmony
items.line: Haskell, from the years when the practice was NLP and data science.

items.name: agda-proofs
items.line: Dependently typed proofs in Agda.
